hook.convey: closed shape → walk its edge from one corner, along every side, back to that same corner → the distance walked = perimeter; a rectangular cricket pitch, the border of a drawing sheet, a fence along a garden bed

use.hi: Cricket pitch ek lamba rectangle hoti hai, 22 m lambi aur 3 m chaudi. Groundsman pitch ke ek kone se chalna shuru kare, kinaare-kinaare chale aur wapas usi kone par pahunche, toh jitna woh chala, wahi pitch ka parimap hai.
use.en: A cricket pitch is a long rectangle, 22 m long and 3 m wide. If the groundsman starts at one corner of the pitch, walks along its edge and comes back to the same corner, the distance he walked is the pitch's perimeter.

use.hi: Drawing sheet ke chaaron kinaaron par colour ki border banao, toh us border ki poori lambai sheet ka parimap hoti hai.
use.en: If you draw a coloured border along all four edges of a drawing sheet, the full length of that border is the sheet's perimeter.

use.hi: Garden mein phoolon ki kyari ke kinaare par baad lagti hai. Baad kyari ki har bhuja ke saath chalti hai, ek bhi bhuja nahi chhootti.
use.en: In a garden, a fence goes along the edge of a flower bed. The fence runs along every side of the bed; not one side is left out.

explain.convey: perimeter (parimap) = total length of the boundary of a closed shape → start at a corner, go along every side, end back at that corner; triangle 4 cm, 5 cm, 6 cm → all three sides go into the sum

point.hi: Is triangle ki teen bhujayein hain: 4 cm, 5 cm aur 6 cm. Ek kone se chalo, teeno bhujaon se hote hue wapas usi kone par aao. Yeh poora raasta hi triangle ka parimap hai.
point.en: This triangle has three sides: 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm. Start at one corner, go along all three sides and come back to the same corner. That whole path is the triangle's perimeter.

prompt.hi: Toh is triangle ka parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: So what is the perimeter of this triangle?

explain.convey: any polygon (bahubhuj) → same rule: add every side, however many; hexagon = 6 sides → 6 lengths in the sum; regular hexagon with only one side labelled 5 cm → the unlabelled sides still belong to the boundary → still added

point.hi: Yeh hexagon hai. Iski chhah bhujayein hain aur sab barabar lambi hain. Label sirf ek bhuja par hai, 5 cm. Baaki bhujaon par kuch likha nahi hai, phir bhi woh kinaare ka hissa hain. Parimap mein har bhuja ki lambai judti hai.
point.en: This is a hexagon. It has six sides and all of them are equally long. Only one side has a label, 5 cm. Nothing is written on the other sides, but they are still part of the edge. In the perimeter every side's length is added.

prompt.hi: Toh is hexagon ka parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: So what is the perimeter of this hexagon?

explain.convey: perimeter = AROUND the shape (a thread along the edge) → a length → cm, m, km; area (kshetrafal) = INSIDE (tiles covering the surface) → a different quantity; 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle → the edge goes 6, 4, 6, 4 → add them, never 6 × 4

point.hi: Yeh rectangle 6 cm lamba aur 4 cm chauda hai. Parimap ek dhaage jaisa hai jo kinaare par chalta hai: upar 6 cm, phir 4 cm, neeche 6 cm, phir 4 cm. Andar ki jagah area hai, woh bilkul alag cheez hai.
point.en: This rectangle is 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. The perimeter is like a thread running along the edge: 6 cm on top, then 4 cm, 6 cm at the bottom, then 4 cm. The space inside is the area, which is a completely different thing.

prompt.hi: Is rectangle ke kinaare par ek baar dhaaga lagana hai. Kitna dhaaga lagega?
prompt.en: A thread goes once along the edge of this rectangle. How much thread is needed?

problem.hi: Ek triangle shape ki phoolon ki kyari hai. Iski bhujayein 7 m, 9 m aur 12 m hain. Kyari ke kinaare-kinaare ek baar baad lagani hai. Kitni lambi baad lagegi?
problem.en: A flower bed is shaped like a triangle. Its sides are 7 m, 9 m and 12 m. A fence goes once along the edge of the bed. How long is the fence?

givens.hi: kyari triangle shape ki hai, ek band shape
givens.en: the flower bed is a triangle, a closed shape

givens.hi: bhujayein 7 m, 9 m aur 12 m hain
givens.en: the sides are 7 m, 9 m and 12 m

find.hi: baad ki lambai, yaani kyari ka parimap
find.en: the length of the fence, that is, the perimeter of the bed

do.hi: Baad kinaare par lagti hai, toh yeh parimap ka sawaal hai. Teeno bhujayein jodni hain.
do.en: The fence goes along the edge, so this is a perimeter question. All three sides must be added.

why.hi: Koi bhi bhuja chhooti toh baad adhoori reh jaayegi.
why.en: If any side is left out, the fence will be incomplete.

do.en: First add two of the sides.

why.hi: Ek kone se chalke do bhujayein poori hui, teesri abhi baaki hai.
why.en: From one corner, two sides are done; the third is still left.

prompt.hi: Ab teesri bhuja, 12 m, bhi jodo. 16 m mein 12 m jodkar kitna hua?
prompt.en: Now add the third side, 12 m, as well. 16 m plus 12 m makes how much?

answer.hi: Toh kyari ke liye 28 m lambi baad lagegi.
answer.en: So the flower bed needs 28 m of fencing.

why.hi: Baad kinaare par chalti hai, isliye parimap. Teeno bhujayein judi, koi nahi chhooti. Jawab ek lambai hai, isliye metre mein aata hai, square metre mein nahi.
why.en: The fence runs along the edge, so it is the perimeter. All three sides were added and none was left out. The answer is a length, so it is in metres, not square metres.

prompt.hi: Ek L-shape kamre ki 6 bhujayein hain. Ek kone se ghoomte hue unki lambai 8 m, 3 m, 5 m, 4 m, 3 m aur 7 m hai. Kamre ka parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: An L-shaped room has 6 sides. Going round from one corner, the sides are 8 m, 3 m, 5 m, 4 m, 3 m and 7 m. What is the perimeter of the room?

prompt.hi: Ek rectangle card ki bhujayein ghoomte hue 10 cm, 4 cm, 10 cm aur 4 cm hain. Iske kinaare par ek baar lace lagani hai. Kitni lace chahiye?
prompt.en: A rectangular card has sides 10 cm, 4 cm, 10 cm and 4 cm going round. Lace goes once along its edge. How much lace is needed?

ladder.why: first straight use: triangle, three given sides → add all
decide perimeter vs area from the situation: lace around vs cloth covering
error-spot: Riya stops at 5 of 6 sides of an L-shape → find the left-out side and the true perimeter
six unequal edges in a real context (exhibition board tape) → every edge, once

remediation.move: named-corner walk instead of a list of numbers: start at A, name each side as its length goes into the sum (AB, BC, … FA); the sum is done only when the walk is back at A

say.hi: Is khet ke kono ke naam A se F tak hain. A se shuru karo, aur har bhuja ka naam aur uski lambai bolo: AB 10 m, BC 4 m, CD 6 m, DE 5 m, EF 4 m, aur aakhir mein FA 9 m. Jod tabhi poora hota hai jab tum wapas A par pahunchte ho.
say.en: The corners of this field are named A to F. Start at A, and say each side's name and its length: AB 10 m, BC 4 m, CD 6 m, DE 5 m, EF 4 m, and last of all FA 9 m. The sum is complete only when you are back at A.

prompt.hi: Ek chhah bhujaon wale khet ABCDEF mein AB = 10 m, BC = 4 m, CD = 6 m, DE = 5 m, EF = 4 m aur FA = 9 m hai. Khet ka parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: A 6-sided field ABCDEF has AB = 10 m, BC = 4 m, CD = 6 m, DE = 5 m, EF = 4 m and FA = 9 m. What is its perimeter?

remediation.move: thread vs tiles on the same rectangle: thread laid along the edge, then straightened against a ruler = perimeter (cm); tiles laid inside = area; a perimeter question → thread, so add the edge lengths one by one, never multiply them

say.hi: Yeh rectangle 5 cm lamba aur 3 cm chauda hai. Iske kinaare par dhaaga lapeto, phir use seedha karke scale par napo, woh parimap hai, cm mein. Andar tiles bichhao toh woh area hai. Parimap ke liye kinaare ki bhujayein jodte hain, 5, 3, 5 aur 3, guna nahi karte.
say.en: This rectangle is 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. Wrap a thread along its edge, then straighten it and measure it on a ruler: that is the perimeter, in cm. Laying tiles inside gives the area. For the perimeter we add the sides of the edge, 5, 3, 5 and 3; we do not multiply.

prompt.hi: 5 cm lambe aur 3 cm chaude label ke kinaare par ek baar ribbon lagta hai. Ribbon kitna lamba hai?
prompt.en: Ribbon goes once around the edge of a label 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. How long is the ribbon?

bridgeToNext.hi: Har bhuja jodna hamesha kaam karta hai. Rectangle mein lambai do baar aati hai aur chaudai bhi do baar, isliye agle hisse mein uska ek chhota tareeka dekhenge.
bridgeToNext.en: Adding every side always works. In a rectangle the length comes twice and the breadth comes twice, so in the next part we will see a shorter way for it.

hook.convey: rectangle and square boundaries everywhere → their sides repeat → a quicker way than writing all four numbers each time

use.hi: Cricket pitch 22 m lambi aur 3 m chaudi hoti hai. Uske kinaare par chalo toh 22 m do baar aata hai aur 3 m bhi do baar. Isi jodi se rectangle ka chhota tareeka banta hai.
use.en: A cricket pitch is 22 m long and 3 m wide. Walk along its edge and 22 m comes twice, and 3 m comes twice too. This pairing gives the rectangle its shortcut.

use.hi: Ludo board ek square hota hai, uski chaaron bhujayein barabar hoti hain. Ek bhuja pata ho, toh poore board ka parimap nikal jaata hai.
use.en: A ludo board is a square; all four of its sides are equal. If you know one side, you can find the perimeter of the whole board.

explain.convey: rectangle (aayat) → opposite sides equal → going round: lambai, chaudai, lambai, chaudai; 10 m by 6 m → the board labels each length once, but the walk passes each twice

point.hi: Is rectangle mein upar aur neeche ki bhuja 10 m ki hai, yeh lambai hai. Daayein aur baayein ki bhuja 6 m ki hai, yeh chaudai hai. Aamne-saamne ki bhujayein barabar hain. Board par 10 m aur 6 m ek-ek baar likha hai, par kinaare par chalte hue lambai do baar aati hai aur chaudai bhi do baar.
point.en: In this rectangle the top and bottom sides are 10 m; that is the length. The right and left sides are 6 m; that is the breadth. Opposite sides are equal. The board writes 10 m and 6 m once each, but walking the edge you pass the length twice and the breadth twice.

prompt.hi: Toh is rectangle ka parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: So what is the perimeter of this rectangle?

explain.convey: one length + one breadth = corner to the opposite corner = HALF the way round; the full round = that half twice → P = 2 × (l + b) = 2 × (10 + 6) = 2 × 16 = 32 m; l + b alone = 16 m = only half the boundary

point.hi: Neeche baayein kone se chalo: 10 m lambai, phir 6 m chaudai, aur tum saamne wale kone par ho. Yeh sirf aadha raasta hai, 10 + 6 = 16 m. Baaki aadha raasta bhi utna hi hai. Isliye rectangle ka parimap = 2 × (lambai + chaudai), yaani 2 × 16 = 32 m.
point.en: Start at the bottom-left corner: 10 m of length, then 6 m of breadth, and you are at the opposite corner. That is only half the way, 10 + 6 = 16 m. The other half is just as long. So a rectangle's perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth), that is 2 × 16 = 32 m.

prompt.hi: Ek rectangle 12 m lamba aur 5 m chauda hai. 2 × (lambai + chaudai) se iska parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: A rectangle is 12 m long and 5 m wide. Using 2 × (length + breadth), what is its perimeter?

explain.convey: square (varg) → all 4 sides equal → side + side + side + side = 4 × side; the answer is a length → cm, not square cm; square of side 6 cm

point.hi: Yeh square hai. Iski chaaron bhujayein 6 cm ki hain, sab barabar. Chaar baar 6 cm jodne ki jagah seedha 4 × bhuja kar sakte ho. Jawab ek lambai hai, isliye cm mein aayega, square cm mein nahi.
point.en: This is a square. All four of its sides are 6 cm, all equal. Instead of adding 6 cm four times, you can just do 4 × side. The answer is a length, so it comes in cm, not square cm.

prompt.hi: Toh is square ka parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: So what is the perimeter of this square?

problem.hi: Ek rectangle notebook cover 24 cm lamba aur 18 cm chauda hai. Iske kinaare par ek baar tape lagani hai. Kitni tape lagegi?
problem.en: A rectangular notebook cover is 24 cm long and 18 cm wide. Tape goes once along its edge. How much tape is needed?

find.hi: tape ki lambai, yaani cover ka parimap
find.en: the length of tape, that is, the perimeter of the cover

do.hi: Tape kinaare par lagti hai, toh parimap chahiye. Cover rectangle hai, toh parimap = 2 × (lambai + chaudai).
do.en: Tape goes along the edge, so we need the perimeter. The cover is a rectangle, so perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth).

why.hi: Kinaare par lambai do baar aati hai aur chaudai bhi do baar.
why.en: Along the edge the length comes twice and the breadth comes twice.

do.hi: Pehle bracket: ek lambai aur ek chaudai jodo.
do.en: Bracket first: add one length and one breadth.

why.hi: 42 cm sirf aadha kinaara hai, ek kone se saamne wale kone tak.
why.en: 42 cm is only half the edge, from one corner to the opposite corner.

prompt.hi: Ab is aadhe kinaare ko do baar lo. 2 × 42 kitna hota hai?
prompt.en: Now take this half-edge twice. What is 2 × 42?

answer.hi: Toh cover par 84 cm tape lagegi.
answer.en: So the cover needs 84 cm of tape.

why.hi: Jaanch ke liye chaaron bhujayein jodo: 24 + 18 + 24 + 18 bhi 84 cm aata hai. 42 cm akela sirf aadha kinaara hai. Aur 24 × 18 = 432 andar ka area hota, kinaara nahi.
why.en: To check, add all four sides: 24 + 18 + 24 + 18 also gives 84 cm. 42 cm alone is only half the edge. And 24 × 18 = 432 would be the area inside, not the edge.

prompt.hi: Ek rectangle playground 40 m lamba aur 25 m chauda hai. Iska parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: A rectangular playground is 40 m long and 25 m wide. What is its perimeter?

prompt.hi: Ek rectangle table mat 9 cm lamba aur 5 cm chauda hai. Iske kinaare par ek baar lace silni hai. Kitni lace chahiye?
prompt.en: Lace is sewn once along the edge of a rectangular table mat 9 cm long and 5 cm wide. How much lace is needed?

prompt.hi: Ek square tile ki bhuja 11 cm hai. Iska parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: A square tile has side 11 cm. What is its perimeter?

ladder.why: direct 2 × (l + b) on a small rectangle, 8 cm by 5 cm
direct 4 × side on a square, in metres
error-spot: Raj's 19 m for a 12 m by 7 m garden = l + b once → name the missing two sides, give 38 m
explain the formula itself: why (l + b) is taken twice
both formulas side by side (square rangoli vs rectangular mat) → compare, spot equal perimeters

remediation.move: ant walk with a running counter instead of a formula: the ant starts at a corner, counter after each side 14 → 20 → 34 → 40 m; l + b = 20 m = the ant only at the opposite corner, halfway; sides walked 4, sides added in l + b only 2

say.hi: Ek cheenti is rectangle ke ek kone se chalti hai, uske paas ek meter hai. 14 m lambai ke baad meter 14 dikhata hai, 6 m chaudai ke baad 20. Ab woh sirf saamne wale kone par hai, aadhe raaste par. Agli lambai ke baad 34, aur aakhri chaudai ke baad 40 m, wapas shuru wale kone par. Cheenti chaar bhujayein chali, lambai + chaudai mein sirf do judti hain.
say.en: An ant starts at one corner of this rectangle and carries a counter. After the 14 m length the counter shows 14, after the 6 m breadth it shows 20. Now the ant is only at the opposite corner, halfway. After the next length it shows 34, and after the last breadth 40 m, back at the starting corner. The ant walked four sides; length + breadth adds only two.

prompt.hi: Ek cheenti 20 m lambe aur 9 m chaude rectangle khet ka ek poora chakkar lagati hai. Aakhir mein uska meter kitna dikhayega?
prompt.en: An ant walks once round a rectangular field 20 m long and 9 m wide. What does its distance counter show at the end?

remediation.move: thread around vs tiles inside the same rectangle: thread along the edge → straightened on a ruler → cm (perimeter); tiles covering → square cm (area); 7 × 3 counts tiles, not thread

say.hi: Yeh rectangle 7 cm lamba aur 3 cm chauda hai. Andar 1 cm ke tiles bichhao toh 7 × 3 = 21 tiles aate hain, woh area hai, square cm mein. Dhaaga kinaare par chalta hai, toh 7, 3, 7 aur 3 ko jodna hai, aur jawab cm mein aata hai.
say.en: This rectangle is 7 cm long and 3 cm wide. Lay 1 cm tiles inside and 7 × 3 = 21 tiles fit; that is the area, in square cm. A thread runs along the edge, so 7, 3, 7 and 3 are added, and the answer is in cm.

prompt.hi: 8 cm lambe aur 2 cm chaude bookmark ke kinaare par ek baar dhaaga lagta hai. Dhaaga kitna lamba hai?
prompt.en: A thread goes once around the edge of a bookmark 8 cm long and 2 cm wide. How long is the thread?

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak humne bhujaon se parimap nikala. Agle hisse mein ulta bhi chalenge: parimap pata ho toh bhuja nikalna, aur chakkar aur baad ka kharcha bhi.
bridgeToNext.en: So far we found the perimeter from the sides. In the next part we will also go backwards, finding a side from the perimeter, and work out rounds and the cost of a fence.

hook.convey: real boundary jobs → perimeter is the first number, then one more step: rounds × perimeter, metres × rate, or perimeter back to a side

use.hi: Football ground ek rectangle hota hai. Uske teen chakkar lagao toh kitna daude, yeh pehle ek chakkar yaani parimap se nikalta hai, phir chakkaron se guna karte hain.
use.en: A football ground is a rectangle. How far you run in three rounds of it comes first from one round, that is the perimeter, and then you multiply by the rounds.

use.hi: Garden ki kyari ke kinaare par taar lagani ho, toh taar metre ke hisaab se bikti hai. Pehle parimap nikalte hain, phir har metre ka daam lagate hain.
use.en: If wire goes along the edge of a garden bed, the wire is sold by the metre. First we find the perimeter, then we apply the price of each metre.

use.hi: Cricket pitch 22 m lambi aur 3 m chaudi hai. Uske kinaare par rassi lagani ho toh pehle parimap nikalte hain, 2 × (22 + 3) = 50 m, phir rassi ka daam.
use.en: A cricket pitch is 22 m long and 3 m wide. To put a rope along its edge, first we find the perimeter, 2 × (22 + 3) = 50 m, then the price of the rope.

explain.convey: backward for a square: perimeter 60 m shared by 4 equal sides → side = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 m; check: 4 × 15 = 60 m

point.hi: Is square ka parimap 60 m hai, aur yeh 60 m chaar barabar bhujaon mein bata hua hai. Isliye ek bhuja = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 m. Jaanch karo: 4 × 15 = 60 m.
point.en: This square's perimeter is 60 m, and that 60 m is shared by four equal sides. So one side = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 m. Check: 4 × 15 = 60 m.

prompt.hi: Ek square ka parimap 40 m hai. Uski ek bhuja kitni lambi hai?
prompt.en: A square has a perimeter of 40 m. How long is one side?

explain.convey: backward for a rectangle: perimeter 60 m, length 20 m → half the perimeter = one length + one breadth = 30 m → breadth = 30 − 20 = 10 m; check: 2 × (20 + 10) = 60 m

point.hi: Is rectangle ka parimap 60 m hai aur lambai 20 m. Aadha parimap, yaani 30 m, ek lambai aur ek chaudai ke barabar hota hai. Toh chaudai = 30 − 20 = 10 m. Jaanch: 2 × (20 + 10) = 60 m.
point.en: This rectangle's perimeter is 60 m and its length is 20 m. Half the perimeter, 30 m, equals one length and one breadth. So the breadth = 30 − 20 = 10 m. Check: 2 × (20 + 10) = 60 m.

prompt.hi: Ek rectangle ka parimap 50 m hai aur lambai 18 m. Iski chaudai kitni hai?
prompt.en: A rectangle has a perimeter of 50 m and a length of 18 m. What is its breadth?

explain.convey: fencing cost = perimeter (m) × rate (₹ per m); 12 m by 8 m plot → 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 m → at ₹10 per m → 40 × 10 = ₹400; a gate or gap with no wire → subtract its length from the perimeter before multiplying

point.hi: Is rectangle plot ki lambai 12 m aur chaudai 8 m hai. Taar poore kinaare par lagegi, toh parimap 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 m. Taar ₹10 per metre hai, toh kharcha 40 × 10 = ₹400. Agar kahin gate ho jahan taar nahi lagti, toh pehle uski lambai parimap se ghatate hain, phir guna karte hain.
point.en: This rectangular plot is 12 m long and 8 m wide. The wire goes along the whole edge, so the perimeter is 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 m. Wire is ₹10 per metre, so the cost is 40 × 10 = ₹400. If there is a gate where no wire goes, we first subtract its length from the perimeter, then multiply.

prompt.hi: Isi plot mein 2 m ka gate hai jahan taar nahi lagegi. Ab kitne metre taar lagegi?
prompt.en: This same plot has a 2 m gate where no wire goes. How many metres of wire are needed now?

problem.hi: Rani 50 m lambe aur 30 m chaude rectangle park ke 3 chakkar daudti hai. Woh kul kitna daudti hai?
problem.en: Rani runs 3 rounds of a rectangular park 50 m long and 30 m wide. How far does she run?

find.hi: Rani kul kitni doori daudti hai

do.hi: Ek chakkar matlab park ke poore kinaare par ek baar daudna, yaani park ka parimap.
do.en: One round means running once along the whole edge of the park, that is, the park's perimeter.

why.hi: Chakkar kinaare par lagta hai, park ke andar nahi.
why.en: A round goes along the edge, not across the inside of the park.

do.hi: Park rectangle hai, toh parimap = 2 × (lambai + chaudai).
do.en: The park is a rectangle, so perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth).

why.hi: Kinaare par lambai do baar aati hai aur chaudai bhi do baar.
why.en: Along the edge the length comes twice and the breadth comes twice.

why.hi: 80 m sirf aadha chakkar hai, ek kone se saamne wale kone tak.
why.en: 80 m is only half a round, from one corner to the opposite corner.

do.hi: Ise do baar lo, tab ek poora chakkar banta hai.
do.en: Take it twice; that makes one full round.

why.hi: Aadha chakkar do baar, toh poora chakkar.
why.en: Half a round twice is a full round.

do.hi: Teeno chakkar barabar hain, toh ek chakkar ko 3 se guna karna hai.
do.en: The three rounds are equal, so one round is multiplied by 3.

why.hi: Har chakkar mein utni hi doori hai, 160 m.
why.en: Every round covers the same distance, 160 m.

prompt.hi: Har chakkar 160 m ka hai aur Rani ne 3 chakkar lagaye. 3 × 160 kitna hota hai?
prompt.en: Each round is 160 m and Rani ran 3 rounds. What is 3 × 160?

answer.hi: Toh Rani kul 480 m daudti hai.
answer.en: So Rani runs 480 m in all.

why.hi: Har chakkar poora kinaara hai, 160 m. Teen barabar chakkar hain, isliye 3 se guna. Agar 3 × (50 + 30) = 240 m karte, toh har baar sirf aadha chakkar judta.
why.en: Each round is the whole edge, 160 m. There are three equal rounds, so multiply by 3. Doing 3 × (50 + 30) = 240 m would add only half a round each time.

prompt.hi: Ek square garden ka parimap 84 m hai. Uski ek bhuja kitni lambi hai?
prompt.en: A square garden has a perimeter of 84 m. How long is one side?

prompt.hi: Ek rectangle khet 30 m lamba aur 20 m chauda hai. Taar ₹15 per metre milti hai. Khet ke kinaare par ek baar taar lagane mein kitna kharcha hoga?
prompt.en: A rectangular field is 30 m long and 20 m wide. Fencing wire costs ₹15 per metre. What does it cost to fence the field once around?

prompt.hi: Ek rectangle rangoli border ka parimap 70 cm hai aur lambai 20 cm. Iski chaudai kitni hai?
prompt.en: A rectangular rangoli border has a perimeter of 70 cm and a length of 20 cm. What is its breadth?

ladder.why: backward for a square: perimeter 400 m → one side
backward for a rectangle: perimeter and length known → halve, then subtract the length
fencing cost: perimeter × ₹ per metre, then the gate variant → subtract 2 m before multiplying

remediation.move: ant walk run backward: full boundary = 2 lengths + 2 breadths; the ant at the opposite corner = half the perimeter = 1 length + 1 breadth; 18 m by 12 m → 60 m round, half = 30 m = 18 + 12 → so halve the perimeter first, then take away the length

say.hi: Is rectangle ki lambai 18 m aur chaudai 12 m hai. Poora chakkar do lambai aur do chaudai hai, 60 m. Cheenti saamne wale kone par pahunche toh aadha raasta hua, 30 m, yaani 18 + 12. Isliye ulta chalte waqt pehle parimap ka aadha karo, phir lambai ghatao.
say.en: This rectangle is 18 m long and 12 m wide. A full round is two lengths and two breadths, 60 m. When the ant reaches the opposite corner it has gone half the way, 30 m, that is 18 + 12. So when going backwards, first halve the perimeter, then take away the length.

prompt.hi: Ek rectangle talaab ka parimap 80 m hai aur lambai 25 m. Iski chaudai kitni hai?
prompt.en: A rectangular pond has a perimeter of 80 m and a length of 25 m. What is its breadth?

remediation.move: wire is bought by the metre of edge, not by the ground inside: thread around the plot vs tiles inside it; cost = edge length (m) × ₹ per m; l × b = ground covered, not wire

say.hi: Is rectangle plot ki lambai 10 m aur chaudai 6 m hai. Taar kinaare par lagti hai, isliye pehle kinaare ki poori lambai metre mein nikalte hain, phir use har metre ke daam se guna karte hain. 10 × 6 = 60 toh andar ki zameen hai, taar nahi.
say.en: This rectangular plot is 10 m long and 6 m wide. Wire goes along the edge, so first we find the full length of the edge in metres, then multiply it by the price of each metre. 10 × 6 = 60 is the ground inside, not the wire.

prompt.hi: ₹20 per metre wali taar 10 m lambe aur 6 m chaude plot ke kinaare par ek baar lagti hai. Taar ka kharcha kitna hai?
prompt.en: Wire costing ₹20 per metre goes once around a plot 10 m long and 6 m wide. What does the wire cost?
